agent.command:
We are recording a one-minute tutorial about the desktop backend of a tool called recording-rig, which records Claude Desktop sessions as GIFs. Present it as three sections. Each section is a bold title followed by exactly ONE plain sentence, and after writing each section call the rig_checkpoint tool with the name given in brackets before writing the next one. Keep the whole reply short enough to fit on one screen.

1. 'What gets recorded' [section-1]: the tool drives this Claude Desktop window through macOS accessibility and captures the window with ScreenCaptureKit, so nothing is scraped from the screen.

2. 'How the driver knows you are done' [section-2]: the model reports progress through the Recording Rig Bridge tools, rig_checkpoint for a named milestone and rig_turn_end when the turn is finished, so the driver never guesses from the UI.

3. 'How the GIF earns its place' [section-3]: a GIF renders only if the bridge transcript holds every required checkpoint in order and ends with rig_turn_end, so a session that quietly went wrong never publishes.

After section 3, write the single line TUTORIAL_COMPLETE and then call the rig_turn_end tool.

system_prompt_prologue: First, load the Recording Rig Bridge tools (rig_checkpoint, rig_turn_end) so they are available. Then do the task below exactly as written, calling rig_checkpoint with the bracketed name after each section, and as your final step call the rig_turn_end tool.
